sections.summary: Standard epistolary greeting identifying the sender as Paul, an apostle by God's will, and the recipients as saints and faithful ones in Christ Jesus, with grace and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

sections.section_title: The Berakah Opens -- Election and Adoption
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds that the election and predestination language describes God's corporate, purposive choosing of a people -- using LXX eklegomai, which consistently designates Israel's corporate election -- to be holy and blameless, with the 'us' referring to Jewish believers in continuity with Israel's election.
sections.relevance: This passage is conventionally cited as proof that God individually predestined specific persons to unconditional eternal security. The neutral reading reveals it is about corporate, purposive election: God chose a people to be holy and for adoption, using Israel's own election vocabulary. The LXX background shows eklegomai is always corporate and purposive -- election TO something (holiness, service, vocation) -- not the selection of isolated individuals to an irrevocable salvific status. The distinction between election to purpose and election to unconditional salvation is critical, and the neutral reading respects it throughout.
key_phrases: he chose us in him before the foundation of the world
that we should be holy and blameless before him
he predestined us for adoption as sons
according to the purpose of his will

sections.section_title: Redemption, the Mystery, and the First to Hope
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this section narrates God's redemptive work (forgiveness through Christ's blood), the disclosure of the cosmic mystery (uniting all things under Christ's headship), the inheritance received, and the identity of 'those who first hoped in Christ' as Jewish believers, all framed within God's eternal purpose.

sections.section_title: The Gentile Inclusion and the Spirit's Seal
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds that the emphatic 'you also' marks the Gentile recipients' inclusion into the story that began with Jewish believers; the Spirit's sealing marks them as belonging to God, and the arrabon (down payment) guarantees that God will complete his plan for the corporate inheritance.
sections.relevance: This passage is conventionally cited as proof that each individual believer is permanently sealed and cannot lose salvation -- the Spirit's guarantee makes the outcome inevitable for every sealed person. The neutral reading reveals the passage is primarily about the mechanism of Gentile inclusion into Israel's corporate inheritance. The seal marks the Gentiles as belonging to God's people, and the arrabon guarantees God's commitment to complete the corporate inheritance plan, not the irrevocability of any individual's participation in it. The three connotations of sealing identified by the neutral reading -- ownership, authentication, and protection -- are all corporate in the LXX background (Ezekiel 9:4-6 marks a group for corporate protection). The guarantee is of God's cosmic plan, not a statement that no individual can defect from the people who hold the inheritance.
key_phrases: were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit
until we acquire possession of it

sections.summary: Paul prays that the recipients would receive a spirit of wisdom and revelation to know the hope of God's calling, the riches of his inheritance in the saints, and the surpassing greatness of his power toward those who believe -- the same power demonstrated in Christ's resurrection.

sections.section_title: Christ's Exaltation and the Assembly as His Body
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this section describes God's power demonstrated in Christ's resurrection and enthronement far above all cosmic powers in every age, and identifies the church as Christ's body and the fullness of the one who fills all things.
